text:
anya: Hey team — draft RN for v1.24.0 is in the doc: https://redwood.docs/rn/v1.24.0. Can reviewers skim for anything that will affect SRE/ops messaging?
kevin: taking a look now. main ask: shorten TL;DR to one sentence + one ops note.
maria: heads up — we need a clear rollback path in the RN. previous rollout hit a db-migration hiccup. pls include exact rollback version + hotfix steps.
anya: good call. added a 'rollback' snippet under 'Operational procedures' with exact commands. excerpt: ```bash
# rollback to previous stable
redwoodctl deploy set-version --service api --version v1.23.7
redwoodctl run-migrations --rollback --tag pre-v1.24
```
sam: I'm scoped to be on-standby during the 03:00 UTC window. I can run the rollback if needed. confirm me in RN ops contacts.
anya: @sam added. Also added an 'expected impact' table with token-rate and latency notes — want to keep it short.
kevin: Suggest we add a single-line 'what to say internally' block for the internal announcement. Ops wants the blast to mention 'no customer-facing changes expected' unless rollback occurs.
maria: +1. Also include contact lines: pager, #eng-oncall, and the fallback email.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled by @anya for 2026-03-22 03:00:00 UTC to cluster-prod-03. Canary window: 15m. Health checks: /health (200) and token-metrics > 95th pct ok.
kevin: Can we pin the RN's header with the short checklist? e.g., 'If canary fails >3 errors/min -> rollback' as an explicit trigger.
anya: done. phrasing: "If canary error rate >3rpm for 10m, rollback to v1.23.7". Is that too aggressive?
sam: that's fine. Also set throttles low for first 10m and watch cached prefixes. I'll monitor kv-cache hit rates and slow callers.
maria: final nit: add a tiny line reminding PMs to hold customer comms until ops confirms stability.
anya: updated doc, pinned internal announce snippet: "Deploying v1.24.0 — infra optimizations; no expected customer changes. Ops standby 03:00 UTC. If canary triggers, rollback to v1.23.7."
kevin: LGTM. I'll post the internal announcement in #general + tag platform leads 30m before. Anyone prefer a different cadence?
sam: 30m is fine. I'll be oncall 15m before and 45m after; set alerting to page at lower thresholds during first hour.
deploy-bot: Reminder queued: will post 'deploy starting' at 2026-03-22 02:30:00 UTC to #eng-releases.
anya: thanks all — final checklist in the RN looks good. If no objections in the next 20m I'll publish the internal blurb and pin the RN. :thumbsup:
